NONCOMPETE VOID NOTIFICATION (BUS. & PROF. CODE § 16600.1(B)) — INFORMATION SHEET AND NOTICE TEMPLATE
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

NOTICE THAT NONCOMPETE CLAUSE IS VOID
NOTICE OF VOID NONCOMPETE CLAUSE

To: Jordan Lee
123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814

From: Acme, Inc.

Date: January 15, 2024

This is written, individualized notice under California Business and Professions Code Section 16600.1(b) regarding the noncompete clause, or noncompete agreement, in the agreement between Jordan Lee and Acme, Inc. dated June 1, 2021. That noncompete clause, or noncompete agreement, is void.

DELIVERY
This notice is being delivered in writing to Jordan Lee's last known address, 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814, and to Jordan Lee's email address, jordan.lee@example.com.

DUTY TO NOTIFY EMPLOYEES THE CLAUSE IS VOID
Separate from the general prohibition on noncompete clauses, California Business and Professions Code Section 16600.1(b)(1) imposes an affirmative notice duty on the employer. For a current employee, and for a former employee who was employed after January 1, 2022, whose contract includes a noncompete clause -- or who was required to enter a noncompete agreement -- that does not satisfy an exception under this chapter, the statute required the employer to notify that employee, by February 14, 2024, that the noncompete clause or noncompete agreement is void. The statute's own text does not prescribe a particular script beyond that content: it requires that the employee be told the clause or agreement is void, not any specific phrasing beyond that.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For current employees, and for former employees who were employed after January 1, 2022, whose contracts include a noncompete clause, or who were required to enter a noncompete agreement, that does not satisfy an exception to this chapter, the employer shall, by February 14, 2024, notify the employee that the noncompete clause or noncompete agreement is void."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16600.1(b)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Business and Professions Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=16600.1.)
  Known gap: This clause describes the notice duty in Section 16600.1(b)(1) only; it does not restate the general prohibition in Section 16600.1(a) or Section 16600, which this document's other clauses on noncompete clauses cover separately -- see this document's clause on enforceability for that text. February 14, 2024 was a fixed, one-time statutory deadline that has already passed as of when this clause was checked; this clause states that historical fact and does not address what follows for an employer that missed it, or whether any obligation continues for employees hired afterward. The statute's own text does not define 'employer' for purposes of this subdivision, and this clause does not resolve whether or how the notice duty applies to any particular employment relationship. Whether a given noncompete clause 'does not satisfy an exception in this chapter' is a separate legal question this clause does not answer.

REQUIRED FORM AND DELIVERY OF THE NOTICE
California Business and Professions Code Section 16600.1(b)(2) specifies the form the required notice must take: a written, individualized communication to the employee or former employee -- not a general announcement or a posted policy update. The statute's own text further specifies that this notice must be delivered to two channels: the employee's or former employee's last known address, and their email address.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Notice made under this subdivision shall be in the form of a written individualized communication to the employee or former employee, and shall be delivered to the last known address and the email address of the employee or former employee."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16600.1(b)(2) (California Legislative Information text), California Business and Professions Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=16600.1.)
  Known gap: The statute's text joins the two delivery channels with 'and,' which on its face calls for delivery to both the last known address and the email address, not either one. This clause does not resolve what the statute requires when one of those channels -- most often a former employee's current email address -- is not known to the employer, or what would satisfy the requirement in that circumstance; the statute's own text does not address it, and no case law resolving that gap has been verified here. This clause covers Section 16600.1(b)(2) only.

CONSEQUENCE OF NOT GIVING THE REQUIRED NOTICE
California Business and Professions Code Section 16600.1(c) states its own enforcement consequence: a violation of Section 16600.1 -- which includes the notice duty in subdivision (b), not only the underlying noncompete prohibition in subdivision (a) -- is, by the statute's own terms, an act of unfair competition within the meaning of Chapter 5 of the Business and Professions Code, commencing with Section 17200.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "A violation of this section constitutes an act of unfair competition within the meaning of Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 17200)."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16600.1(c) (California Legislative Information text), California Business and Professions Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=16600.1.)
  Known gap: This clause confirms only that Section 16600.1 itself makes a violation an act of unfair competition under Chapter 5 (Section 17200 et seq.); it does not summarize what remedies, penalties, or procedures Chapter 5 itself provides for an act of unfair competition, including whether a private right of action, restitution, or civil penalties are available on these facts -- that is a separate body of law this clause does not cover. It also does not address whether subdivision (c) applies to a violation of subdivision (a) alone, subdivision (b) alone, or both, beyond what the statute's plain text states.

SIGNATURE
Acme, Inc.

By: _________________________
Date: January 15, 2024

—
